title: Prepare thermodynamic input data
action: Obtain the thermodynamic parameters (free energy changes ΔG, excess free energies Ω, interfacial energy σ_I, molar surface density ψ) for the Fe-Cr-Ni-Mo-C-N system from the SGTE CALPHAD database (via pycalphad or similar) and a lattice parameter (e.g., 3.60 Å). Convert the supplied variant compositions (weight percent) to mole fractions for each element.
description: Gather all needed numerical inputs: ΔG^(γ→ζ)_(sub) for Fe,Cr,Ni,Mo, ΔG^(γ→ζ)_(int)C, ΔG^(γ→ζ)_(int)N, excess Ω terms, interfacial energy, and molar surface density. The evidence log records the parameters extracted or commands used.

title: Compute SFE for all variants at room temperature and 1323 K
action: Implement the modified thermodynamic model (based on the upgrade to the Curtze et al. formalism, incorporating Mo as a BCC-stabilizing substitutional element, treating C and N as independent interstitial species, and extending to high temperatures) using the parameters from Step 1. For each variant (7N, 11N, 22N), compute the stacking fault energy (γ_SFE) at 298 K and 1323 K. Write the results to sfe_results.csv, one row per variant.
description: Perform the SFE calculation using the mole fractions derived from the given compositions. The model accounts for: substitutional bulk free energy (including Mo terms), separate interstitial contributions from C and N, magnetic and segregation terms, and temperature-dependent terms from the SGTE database. Output a CSV with exactly three rows (one per variant).
output_schema: Columns: variant (string), SFE_RT (float, mJ/m²), SFE_1323K (float, mJ/m²). One row per variant.
